theorem: For arbitrary complex v0,v2 with U=|v0|^2, V=|v2|^2 and A0=1+U+V, if A0/(1+A0*U)<=3, then the explicitly defined 4x4 PPT projection R_v of the source grid state has SN<=2. In particular this holds for EVERY v2 whenever |v0|^2>=1/3, an unbounded two-complex-parameter family. If additionally 3V<4, the state is entangled and therefore has SN exactly2. This strictly extends the prior 3x3-Gram sufficient domain and does not assert a global 4x4 theorem.
source_and_map: Use R=[A]+[B]+[D]+3([C]+[E]+[F]+[G]+[I]+[H0]) as explicitly defined and certified PPT/SN3 in frontier-20261028-grid-state-five-projections-v1.json SHA256 9863760e2ca2331164d12e62300f3ad7db5b6a17a3ef424e360d504d541004a9, based on Krebs–Gachechiladze https://arxiv.org/html/2509.07086v1 Eq.11. Let K|0,1,2>=|0,1,2>, K|3>=v0|0>+v2|2>, K|4>=|3>. Then R_v=(I tensor K)R(I tensor K)^*, ker K=span{|3>-v0|0>-v2|2>}, trace(R_v)=25+6(U+V), and R_v is PPT by local congruence.
phase_construction: For s in C define W=-X+s(F'-v0X)=-|20>+s*v2|22>. For each z^4=1 define q_z=zA'+B'+z^2 D'+z^3 W. It has zero fourth Alice row and zero fourth Bob column; the determinant of its upper 3x3 block is identically zero. Explicit rows are [z,1,0], [z^2,z,1], [-z^3,-z^2,z+z^3*s*v2], whose determinant vanishes for every complex z,s,v2. Hence SR(q_z)<=2. Phase orthogonality gives (1/4)sum_z[q_z]=[A']+[B']+[D']+[W].
gram_decomposition: In the basis (E',G',I',F'), W has coefficient vector t=(-(1+s*v0),(1+s*v0)*v0,(1+s*v0)*v2,s). Therefore R_v=(1/4)sum_z[q_z]+3([C']+[H0'])+sum_(j,k)(3I_4-t t^*)_jk |L_j><L_k|, where L=(E',G',I',F'). All L_j are supported on Alice rows2,3, so every complex linear combination has SR<=2. If ||t||^2<=3, the 4x4 Gram matrix is PSD and its spectral decomposition gives a nonnegative SR<=2 sum.
optimum_and_domain: ||t||^2=A0|1+s*v0|^2+|s|^2. Its exact minimum over complex s is A0/(1+A0 U), achieved at s=-A0*conjugate(v0)/(1+A0 U). Therefore the stated domain gives a valid decomposition. If U>=1/3 then A0(1-3U)<=0<=3, so the domain holds for arbitrary V, however large. For U<1/3 the equivalent bound is V<=3/(1-3U)-1-U. Negative Gram outside this sufficient domain does not imply SN>2.
entanglement: For v2!=0, the actual Alice/Bob 0,1,2 core has range [[a,b,c],[d,a,b],[e+v0*f,-d,a+v2*f]] with unique a,b,c,d,e,f. A rank-one vector satisfies 2a^2=-v2*a*f by two 2x2 minors; after summing any separable decomposition, Cauchy-Schwarz gives 2<=sqrt(3)|v2| from exact moments sum|a|^2=1,sum|f|^2=3. Hence 3V<4 proves entanglement. If v2=0, the extra F' is only a multiple of |20>, and the simpler two-minor range criterion forces a=0 for every rank-one core vector while A belongs to its range, so the state is entangled. With the SR2 decomposition, all stated entangled cases have SN exactly2.
example_beyond_previous_gram: At v0=2,v2=1, the old 3x3-Gram criterion from frontier-20261028-grid-three-head-compressions-v1.json fails: (1+|v2|^2+|v0|^2)/3=2>1. Here A0=6, s=-12/25 and ||t||^2=6/25<3; 3|v2|^2=3<4. Thus rho=R_v/55 is an actual 4x4 PPT entangled SN2 state with kernel |3>-2|0>-|2>, established by the NEW four-generator Gram rather than the previous certificate.

verification.actual: Five Gaussian-rational inputs (v0,v2)=(2,1),(1,2),(i,1),(0,1),(0,2) checked all four rank2 phase vectors and all 256 state entries exactly. For (2,1), residual Gram Schur pivots [1874/625,2805/937,5607/1870,1725/623] and state-PT pivots [1,1,3,3,2/3,1,12,1,12,3] are nonnegative. At (0,2) the residual Gram is not PSD, while the state identity and PT check still pass; this is a certificate failure, not a Schmidt-number counterexample.

limits: This is the v1=0, lambda=0 projection chart and the stated Gram domain only. The entanglement condition 3V<4 is sufficient, not necessary. General Bob kernel directions, arbitrary 4x4 PPT states, a target SN>=3 witness, independent scientific peer review and novelty remain open.
